newsitem.title: GERMANY: German rate cut hopes fade on money supply growth.
newsitem.headline: German rate cut hopes fade on money supply growth.

text.p: Lingering hopes for another easing in German interest rates receded further Thursday after news of a slight pick-up in money supply growth and in business confidence in August.

Meanwhile, as expected, the Bundesbank held its three key interest rates steady at its regular fortnightly meeting, setting its main money market rate, or repo, at an unchanged 3 percent for the next three weeks.
M3 money supply, which the Bundesbank sees as its most important indicator of inflationary trends, grew at an annualized rate of 8.7 percent, compared with 8.6 percent in July.

The figure was well above analysts' forecasts of about 8 percent and marked the first acceleration in growth since February. The Bundesbank said the rise was partly explained by buoyant bank lending, a sign of increasing economic activity.
Economists said the data suggested there was no need for another credit easing in the current economic cycle but stressed that any monetary tightening remained far off.
